reason: E1 shows that hot-press sintering a Hf coating on VZrHfNbTa forms a ~120 μm coating with a HfZr interdiffusion layer, supporting the first two premises. However, E1 provides no evidence on oxidation behavior, HfO2 scale formation, oxygen barrier effectiveness, or retention of mechanical properties, leaving the remaining premises unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: A thin Hf coating can be applied to HfNbTaTiZr by hot-press sintering
Zr from the substrate diffuses into the Hf coating to form a HfZr transition layer
The Hf coating oxidizes to a dense, adherent HfO2 scale that acts as an oxygen barrier
The interdiffused layer ensures mechanical continuity and preserves ductility and yield strength
The coating significantly reduces oxidation weight gain vs. uncoated alloy at 1000 °C in air
